bibl.title: How Can Single Sensory Neurons Predict Behavior?

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: why SINGLE SENSORY NEURONS CAN BE SURPRISINGLY PREDICTIVE OF BEHAVIOR IN DISCRIMINATION TASKS
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: which of two accounts is right, given that BOTH SUBOPTIMAL DECODING AND INFORMATION-LIMITING NOISE CORRELATIONS COULD EXPLAIN THESE TWO PUZZLING PHENOMENA - WHICH IS THE CORRECT EXPLANATION?
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: a pair of quantitative predictions that separate the two accounts, and the finding that CHOICE CORRELATIONS CAN BE USED TO ASSESS THE EFFICIENCY OF THE DOWNSTREAM READ-OUT AND DETECT THE PRESENCE OF INFORMATION-LIMITING CORRELATIONS
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanism
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: choice correlations between sensory neurons and perceptual decisions
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: electrophysiology
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Noise correlations aligned with the stimulus-induced change in mean firing (differential correlations) are indistinguishable from real signal, so pooling cannot average them away; population information saturates and single-neuron thresholds stay close to the behavioral threshold, producing large choice correlations.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A decoder blind to correlations fails to cancel the shared noise fluctuations, so the animal's choice is driven by that irrelevant common noise and every neuron sharing it becomes correlated with the choice.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: An undecoded population inherits information-limiting noise that is partially shared with the decoded population but of larger amplitude, which inflates its choice correlations above the optimal prediction while it contributes nothing to the decision.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: under optimal decoding THE CHOICE CORRELATIONS TAKE THE REMARKABLY SIMPLE FORM OF A RATIO OF DISCRIMINATION THRESHOLDS - and this prediction HAS NO FREE PARAMETERS
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the information cannot be created downstream: IF INFORMATION IS NOT AVAILABLE AT THE INPUT, THEN IT CANNOT BE CREATED LATER BY ADDING MORE NEURONS - THOSE EXTRA NEURONS MAY APPEAR TO ADD MORE SIGNAL STRENGTH, BUT THEY ALSO INHERIT NOISE WITH THE SAME STRUCTURE AS THE SIGNAL
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: and that noise cannot be pooled away: THESE INFORMATION-LIMITING CORRELATIONS CANNOT BE AVERAGED AWAY BY APPROPRIATELY POOLING MANY NEURONS, BECAUSE THESE NOISE FLUCTUATIONS ARE INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM CHANGES IN NEURAL ACTIVITY INDUCED BY A REAL SIGNAL
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: ONLY NOISE CORRELATIONS THAT MIMIC THE EFFECT OF THE STIMULUS ON POPULATION ACTIVITY LEAD TO SIGNIFICANT CHOICE CORRELATIONS - called DIFFERENTIAL CORRELATIONS BECAUSE THE CORRELATIONS MIMIC THE RELEVANT SIGNAL WHICH IS THE DIFFERENTIAL (DERIVATIVE) OF THE MEAN RESPONSES
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Measurement noise leaves open other classes of suboptimal decoder that were not tested
span.note: what this limits: the decoder conclusion: IT REMAINS POSSIBLE THAT NEURAL PROCESSING IS EVEN BETTER DESCRIBED BY SOME OTHER CLASS OF SUBOPTIMAL DECODERS THAT WE DID NOT CONSIDER
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The conclusions depend on the specific class of suboptimal (correlation-blind) decoders considered
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 0: THESE RESULTS DEPEND ON THE PARTICULAR CLASS OF SUBOPTIMAL DECODERS WE CONSIDERED ... NAMELY THE CORRELATION-BLIND DECODERS
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: A decoder that removes only the noisiest mode cannot be definitively excluded
span.note: what this limits: the noisiest-mode argument specifically: WE CANNOT DEFINITIVELY RULE IT OUT
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The optimality test depends on measuring neural thresholds from signals that are not known to be the ones driving behavior
span.note: what this limits: the optimality test itself: IDEALLY, WE WOULD LIKE TO COMPUTE NEURAL THRESHOLDS FROM THE SAME NEURAL SIGNALS THAT DRIVE THE BEHAVIOR, BUT WE DON'T KNOW PRECISELY WHAT THOSE SIGNALS ARE
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the quantity the whole account turns on is not directly measurable - INFORMATION-LIMITING CORRELATIONS ARE DIFFICULT TO ESTIMATE DIRECTLY, REQUIRING LARGE SIMULTANEOUS RECORDINGS WITH MANY TRIALS, and EXTRAPOLATING THE FULL NOISE CORRELATIONS FROM A SPARSE SUBSET OF PAIRWISE CORRELATION MEASUREMENTS IS EXTREMELY DIFFICULT, AND MISTAKES CAN RADICALLY CHANGE THE ESTIMATED INFORMATION CONTENT
span.note: what this limits: any claim about the information content of a population built from pairwise correlation measurements
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the conclusion is relative to one family of alternatives - THESE RESULTS DEPEND ON THE PARTICULAR CLASS OF SUBOPTIMAL DECODERS WE CONSIDERED IN THE EXTENSIVE INFORMATION CASE, NAMELY THE CORRELATION-BLIND DECODERS, which is QUITE GENERAL, ALTHOUGH NOT ALL-ENCOMPASSING
span.note: what this limits: the suboptimality conclusion, which is relative to one family: THESE RESULTS DEPEND ON THE PARTICULAR CLASS OF SUBOPTIMAL DECODERS WE CONSIDERED ... NAMELY THE CORRELATION-BLIND DECODERS
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: DUE TO MEASUREMENT NOISE IN THE DATA, IT REMAINS POSSIBLE THAT NEURAL PROCESSING IS EVEN BETTER DESCRIBED BY SOME OTHER CLASS OF SUBOPTIMAL DECODERS THAT WE DID NOT CONSIDER
span.note: duplicate of: limitations[0] · what this limits: the same scope as item 0 - DUE TO MEASUREMENT NOISE IN THE DATA, IT REMAINS POSSIBLE THAT NEURAL PROCESSING IS EVEN BETTER DESCRIBED BY SOME OTHER class of decoder
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: and the authors say the model cannot be forced to fail - WE CAN ALWAYS CONCOCT SOME COMBINATION OF CORRELATIONS AND SUBOPTIMAL DECODERS THAT WOULD BE CONSISTENT WITH FINE DETAILS OF OUR MEASUREMENTS, rejected on the ground that it WOULD REQUIRE UNPALATABLE FINE-TUNING OF THE MODEL
span.note: what this limits: treating the conclusion as an exclusion rather than as a parsimony judgment
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the two hypotheses are only separable if the sample is diverse enough - THE PREDICTIONS FOR OPTIMAL DECODING COULD BE SATISFIED EVEN FOR A POPULATION OF NEURONS DECODED SUBOPTIMALLY, LEADING US TO MISCHARACTERIZE A SUBOPTIMAL SYSTEM AS OPTIMAL, and THAT NEARLY HAPPENS FOR A HOMOGENEOUS POPULATION
span.note: what this limits: applying the test in a preparation whose tuning curves are not heterogeneous
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: one monkey's data did not decide anything - CHOICE CORRELATIONS FOR MSTd IN THE OTHER MONKEY WERE INCONCLUSIVE
span.note: what this limits: the MSTd evidence specifically: CHOICE CORRELATIONS FOR MSTd IN THE OTHER MONKEY WERE INCONCLUSIVE
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: a result of this paper is that an elegant earlier method may not work - SUCH A FULL RECONSTRUCTION MAY NOT BE FEASIBLE IN THE PRESENCE OF INFORMATION-LIMITING CORRELATIONS, and IT MAY NOT BE POSSIBLE TO USE CHOICE PROBABILITIES TO COMPUTE DECODING WEIGHTS FROM EXPERIMENTAL DATA
span.note: what this limits: the earlier weight-reconstruction method, which this result bears on: DESPITE THE ELEGANCE OF THIS RESULT, ONE CONSEQUENCE OF OUR FI[ndings is that] SUCH A FULL RECONSTRUCTION MAY NOT BE [possible]
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THE DATA PROCESSING INEQUALITY, used to rule out a model of cortical coding outright - THE EXTENSIVE INFORMATION MODEL ATTRIBUTES MORE INFORMATION TO THE CORTEX THAN TO THE SENSORS, AND THIS IS PROHIBITED
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the Akaike Information Criterion, used to choose between five predictors of the same measurements - and OUR DATA WAS STRONG ENOUGH TO SIGNIFICANTLY DIFFERENTIATE BETWEEN THE MODELS
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the whole discrimination procedure run first on simulated populations whose decoder was known
span.note: eliminates: the method not being able to tell the two hypotheses apart at all - IN ALL FOUR MODEL SYSTEMS, THIS METHOD WAS ABLE TO RECOVER THE TRUE VALUES OF BOTH COEFFICIENTS WITHIN THE SIMULATED EXPERIMENTAL UNCERTAINTY · outcome: held
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: three further optimality signatures checked, each of which could have failed
span.note: eliminates: optimality being read off one fit - uninformative neurons had choice correlations NO MORE THAN EXPECTED BY CHANCE, NO NEURONS HAVE A THRESHOLD LOWER THAN THE ANIMAL'S BEHAVIORAL THRESHOLD, and negative choice correlations excluded zero for ONLY 4/339 RECORDED CELLS
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: a neuron-antineuron correction applied to the neural thresholds that an earlier study omitted
span.note: eliminates: NO NEURONS HAVE A THRESHOLD LOWER THAN THE ANIMAL'S BEHAVIORAL THRESHOLD, AS LONG AS NEURAL THRESHOLDS ARE PROPERLY CORRECTED FOR USE OF A NEURON-ANTINEURON PAIR - A CORRECTION THAT WAS NOT APPLIED IN ( COHEN AND NEWSOME 2009 )
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: model quality scored by AIC against a null model and three alternatives
span.note: eliminates: a better fit bought with free parameters - and OUR DATA WAS STRONG ENOUGH TO SIGNIFICANTLY DIFFERENTIATE BETWEEN THE MODELS
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: choice probability
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: threshold
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: efficiency
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: noise fluctuations → real signal
span.note: PROVED INDISTINGUISHABLE - the FORMAL form (Q-286/Q-287). Not 'we could not tell them apart' but 'they cannot be told apart'. AND IT SURVIVES THE OBVIOUS REMEDY: 'these information-limiting correlations CANNOT BE AVERAGED AWAY by appropriately pooling many neurons, BECAUSE these noise fluctuations are indistinguishable from changes in neural activity induced by a real signal'. The indistinguishability is the REASON pooling fails, so it is load-bearing for the paper's conclusion rather than a caveat on it.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THE LARGEST CORRELATION WITH CHOICE SITS IN THE AREA THAT DOES NOT MATTER: REVERSIBLE CHEMICAL INACTIVATION OF VIP DOES NOT IMPAIR HEADING DISCRIMINATION, DESPITE THE FACT THAT VIP NEURONS EXHIBIT LARGE CHOICE CORRELATIONS - and the same holds in another area, ANOTHER RECENT STUDY OF THE PARIETAL CORTEX (AREA LIP) ALSO REPORTS HIGH CHOICE CORRELATIONS, YET INACTIVATING THIS REGION AGAIN HAS NO DISCERNIBLE EFFECT ON VISUAL MOTION DISCRIMINATION
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: and the paper's own summary says the same in its own voice: VIP EXHIBITS HIGH CHOICE PROBABILITIES AND ROBUST NOISE CORRELATIONS MUCH LIKE VN/CN, YET OUR ANALYSIS SUGGESTS THAT VIP IS DECODED SUBOPTIMALLY, IF AT ALL
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THE FIELD'S STANDARD MEASURE OF A NEURON'S INVOLVEMENT IS THEREFORE NOT A MEASURE OF INVOLVEMENT: the brain LOSES VERY LITTLE INFORMATION BY IGNORING VIP, and the choice correlations there are the largest of the three areas
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THE PAPER STATES THE RULE THIS PROJECT CALLS WITHIN-RUN COMPARISONS ONLY: IF DIFFERENT BRAIN REGIONS SEEM TO HAVE DIFFERENT CHOICE CORRELATIONS, ONE MUST TAKE CARE TO ACCOUNT FOR DIFFERENCES IN PSYCHOPHYSICAL SENSITIVITY BETWEEN ANIMALS BEFORE CONCLUDING THAT THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN BRAIN AREAS IS MEANINGFUL - THE SUREST DIAGNOSTIC WOULD BE TO MEASURE CHOICE CORRELATIONS FROM MULTIPLE AREAS WITHIN A SINGLE ANIMAL. The measure has the animal's own threshold in its denominator
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THE SAME NUMBER MEANS OPTIMAL OR SUBOPTIMAL DEPENDING ON A CONSTANT: SUCH A PATTERN OF CHOICE CORRELATIONS INDICATES OPTIMAL DECODING IF AND ONLY IF THE PROPORTIONALITY CONSTANT EQUALS THE THRESHOLD OF POPULATION ACTIVITY - ALL OTHER VALUES OF THE PROPORTIONALITY CONSTANT REFLECT SUBOPTIMAL DECODING. The pattern alone is not the finding
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: and a scale above one is diagnostic of the opposite of what it looks like: CHOICE CORRELATIONS PROPORTIONAL BUT NOT EQUAL TO THE OPTIMAL PREDICTION OCCUR ONLY WITH SOME DEGREE OF SUBOPTIMAL DECODING - WHENEVER THE CHOICE CORRELATIONS HAVE β ≠1, THE EFFICIENCY IS LESS THAN 1
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THE COUNTER-INTUITIVE CASE, WORKED OUT: choice correlations LARGER than the optimal prediction arise WHEN BEHAVIOR IS DRIVEN BY ANOTHER, MORE INFORMATIVE, SOURCE OF SENSORY SIGNALS BESIDE THE NEURAL POPULATION UNDER STUDY - a neuron can be perfectly correlated with a choice it plays no part in
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: TWO HYPOTHESES ARE ONLY DISTINGUISHABLE IF THE SAMPLE IS DIVERSE: THE PREDICTIONS FOR OPTIMAL DECODING COULD BE SATISFIED EVEN FOR A POPULATION OF NEURONS DECODED SUBOPTIMALLY, LEADING US TO MISCHARACTERIZE A SUBOPTIMAL SYSTEM AS OPTIMAL, and THAT NEARLY HAPPENS FOR A HOMOGENEOUS POPULATION. The discriminating power of the test is a property of the sample, not of the theory
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AND AN EARLIER RESULT HOLDS ONLY UNDER ITS OWN IDEALISATION: WEAK POSITIVE NOISE CORRELATIONS DO NOT ALWAYS PRODUCE LARGE CHOICE CORRELATIONS - THIS IS ONLY TRUE FOR THE MODEL THEY CONSIDER WITH HOMOGENEOUS NEURONS AND HOMOGENEOUS NOISE CORRELATIONS
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: A MODEL RULED OUT BY A MATHEMATICAL LAW RATHER THAN BY DATA: SINCE CORTICAL POPULATIONS ARE MUCH LARGER THAN THE SENSORY POPULATION BUT NOT MUCH NOISIER, THE EXTENSIVE INFORMATION MODEL ATTRIBUTES MORE INFORMATION TO THE CORTEX THAN TO THE SENSORS - AND THIS IS PROHIBITED BY THE DATA PROCESSING INEQUALITY
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: and one hypothesis killed by an order-of-magnitude argument: THE CHOICE CORRELATIONS WOULD THEN BE CORRESPONDINGLY TINY, AND MOST LIKELY NOT SIGNIFICANTLY DIFFERENT FROM ZERO GIVEN TYPICAL MEASUREMENT UNCERTAINTY - THIS ARGUMENT RULES OUT MODELS IN WHICH THE BRAIN HAS EXTENSIVE INFORMATION AND DECODES IT OPTIMALLY
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: TWO CONVENTIONAL EXPECTATIONS REVERSED. First: CHOICE CORRELATION SHOULD BE SMALLER FOR LARGER POPULATIONS SINCE INFORMATION IS DISTRIBUTED ACROSS MORE NEURONS - HOWEVER, IF THE CODE IS REDUNDANT AND DECODED NEAR-OPTIMALLY, THEN THE CHOICE CORRELATIONS DO NOT VARY WITH POPULATION SIZE
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Second, and it can invert: CHOICE CORRELATIONS SHOULD BE GREATER WHEN NOISE CORRELATIONS ARE LARGER - THIS IS TRUE ONLY FOR A SPECIFIC PATTERN OF CORRELATIONS, OR FOR CERTAIN TYPES OF DECODERS, and CHOICE CORRELATIONS COULD POTENTIALLY RISE EVEN WHILE THE TOTAL NOISE CORRELATION FALLS
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: OPTIMALITY IS CHEAP AND THE PAPER SAYS SO: ACHIEVING NEAR-OPTIMAL PERFORMANCE MAY NOT BE SUCH AN IMPRESSIVE FEAT, AS OUR RESULTS IMPLY THAT THE INFORMATION ENCODED IN NEURAL POPULATIONS IS HIGHLY REDUNDANT AND THEREFORE ROBUST TO SUBOPTIMAL DECODING - OPTIMALITY MEASURES THE QUALITY OF DECODING, RATHER THAN THE PARTICULAR NETWORK STRUCTURE USED TO DECODE
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: so the label does not identify the mechanism: A BROAD RANGE OF DECODERS MAY ALL PRODUCE SIMILAR NEAR-OPTIMAL PERFORMANCE, and THE TRUE DECODING WEIGHTS COULD RESEMBLE THOSE OF A CORRELATION-BLIND DECODER, OR MANY OTHER DECODERS, AND YET BE NEAR-OPTIMAL
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THE QUANTITY THE ARGUMENT TURNS ON CANNOT BE MEASURED DIRECTLY: INFORMATION-LIMITING CORRELATIONS ARE DIFFICULT TO ESTIMATE DIRECTLY, THE INFORMATION-LIMITING COMPONENT CAN BE VERY SMALL YET HAVE ENORMOUS EFFECTS ON POPULATION INFORMATION, and MISTAKES CAN RADICALLY CHANGE THE ESTIMATED INFORMATION CONTENT OF A NEURAL POPULATION - so it is inferred from an INDIRECT CONSEQUENCE observable with single neurons
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: and it is invisible by construction: INFORMATION-LIMITING NOISE CORRELATIONS MAY HIDE ESSENTIALLY UNNOTICED AMONGST OTHER NOISE CORRELATIONS WITH HIGHER VARIANCE THAT ARISE DOWNSTREAM, because THESE NOISE FLUCTUATIONS ARE INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM CHANGES IN NEURAL ACTIVITY INDUCED BY A REAL SIGNAL
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: A PREDICTION WITH NO FREE PARAMETERS, AND THE AUTHORS SAY SO: THE RATIO OF PSYCHOPHYSICAL TO NEURAL THRESHOLDS DID A REASONABLE JOB OF PREDICTING THE MEASURED CHOICE CORRELATIONS - WE EMPHASIZE THAT THIS PREDICTION HAS NO FREE PARAMETERS
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: AN ADMISSION THAT THE MODEL CANNOT BE FORCED TO FAIL: WE CAN ALWAYS CONCOCT SOME COMBINATION OF CORRELATIONS AND SUBOPTIMAL DECODERS THAT WOULD BE CONSISTENT WITH FINE DETAILS OF OUR MEASUREMENTS - HOWEVER, THIS WOULD REQUIRE UNPALATABLE FINE-TUNING OF THE MODEL. The conclusion is a parsimony judgment and is labelled as one
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: THE INFORMATION CANNOT BE MANUFACTURED DOWNSTREAM: IF INFORMATION IS NOT AVAILABLE AT THE INPUT, THEN IT CANNOT BE CREATED LATER BY ADDING MORE NEURONS - THOSE EXTRA NEURONS MAY APPEAR TO ADD MORE SIGNAL STRENGTH, BUT THEY ALSO INHERIT NOISE WITH THE SAME STRUCTURE AS THE SIGNAL
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: and the empirical answer: THE RESULTANT REGRESSION COEFFICIENTS ON THE SUBOPTIMAL PREDICTORS WERE NEAR ZERO, WHEREAS THOSE ON OPTIMAL PREDICTORS WERE CLOSE TO ONE - THE INFORMATION AVAILABLE IN THE VESTIBULAR AND CEREBELLAR NUCLEI IS USED NEAR-OPTIMALLY, AND BEHAVIORAL PERFORMANCE IS LIMITED PRIMARILY BY CORRELATED NOISE, NOT SUBOPTIMAL DECODING
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

However, OUR RESULTS INSTEAD FAVOR NEAR-OPTIMAL DECODING, for which most correlations play little role.'
